programme: NFYB anchors the promoter-proximal machinery of MHC class II antigen presentation (its regulon includes CIITA, RFX5, CD74, HLA-E — the core components of the MHC-II transactivation/enhanceosome system); AKNA drives the paired CD40/CD40LG costimulatory ligand-receptor pair; ZBTB16 (PLZF) carries a distinct but adjacent regulon of megakaryocyte/platelet genes (MPL, GP1BA, GP9 — thrombopoietin receptor and the GPIb-IX platelet adhesion receptor). Together these three regulons span the antigen-presentation/costimulation/platelet-production interface that governs how immune cells and platelets engage vascular and stromal surfaces.
role_in_a: In gastric cancer, all three factors are independently documented: NFYB overexpression reprograms tumor stroma and predicts worse survival (PMID 36152055); AKNA and ZBTB16 both behave as tumor suppressors whose loss (AKNA directly, ZBTB16 via lncRNA-mediated repression) promotes progression (PMID 32462010, PMID 35451560). Read together, the axis fits a tumor-immune-evasion/stromal-remodeling picture: loss of costimulatory (CD40/CD40LG) and platelet-lineage (ZBTB16) signaling removes checks on tumor growth while NFYB-driven MHC-II regulon activity is co-opted to reshape the stroma rather than to present antigen effectively.
role_in_b: None of the three factors have a retrieved paper or an Open Targets association in stroke in this record. Mechanistically, the same regulon would be expected to matter in blood: CD40LG is stored in platelet alpha-granules and released on activation to engage CD40 on endothelium and leukocytes (thromboinflammation), and MPL/GP1BA/GP9 govern platelet production and the GPIb-IX adhesion receptor central to arterial thrombus formation — both classic contributors to atherothrombotic ischemic stroke. This role is inferred from general platelet biology, not from anything retrieved for this pair.
shared_axis: A costimulatory/platelet-lineage programme that is silenced or co-opted in gastric tumor progression (AKNA, ZBTB16 loss; NFYB gain) would, in blood, correspond to the platelet CD40L-release and glycoprotein-receptor programme that drives arterial thrombosis in stroke. That the two 'stroke' network cohorts are built from blood rather than brain tissue is consistent with this reading, since platelet biology is directly assayed there. The discordant direction flags on AKNA and ZBTB16 (51/90 and 49/90, vs. NFYB's cleaner 61/90) are compatible with a programme running in opposite directions in the two diseases — lost in the tumor, gained in the activated platelet — but that is a plausible reading, not a demonstrated one.
reasoning: The module is nameable and internally consistent (MHC-II regulon, CD40/CD40LG pair, and platelet glycoprotein/thrombopoietin genes are all recognized biological units), and all three carrying factors are independently placed in gastric cancer by direct citations. But nothing in the retrieved record places any of them in stroke — no papers, no Open Targets signal — so the stroke side of the account rests entirely on general platelet/thromboinflammation biology rather than anything retrieved here, capping this at moderate rather than strong.
support: PMID 36152055 — NFYB overexpression reprograms gastric cancer stroma and predicts worse survival; PMID 32462010 — AKNA is a deregulated tumor suppressor in gastric cancer; PMID 35451560 — lncRNA ELFN1-AS1 represses ZBTB16 to promote gastric cancer progression. No PMIDs in the material address any of NFYB, AKNA, or ZBTB16 in stroke.
how_to_falsify: In a megakaryocyte/platelet model (e.g. CHRF-288-11 cells or primary CD34+-derived megakaryocytes), knock down AKNA and ZBTB16 together and measure surface CD40LG and MPL/GP1BA/GP9 transcript and platelet-release-assay output; if their expression does not co-vary, the proposed shared costimulation-platelet module does not hold together as a single programme. Separately, if silencing AKNA in a gastric cancer line does not alter CD40LG-dependent costimulatory signaling to immune cells in coculture, the tumor-side role is also unsupported.
caveats: Tissue pairing is blood for stroke vs. stomach for the cancer, so any platelet-relevant signal in the stroke network is a blood/circulating-cell readout, not a cerebrovascular-tissue one — this favors the platelet reading but means the account says nothing about brain-resident neuroinflammation. Only 2 independent cohort pairs underlie the 90 patient-group comparisons, so the comparisons are not 90 independent replicates. AKNA and ZBTB16 are flagged discordant (opposite-direction target-set agreement) in roughly half their supporting groups, weaker than NFYB's concordant signal. STAT1, a plausible immune master regulator for this story, was excluded as tissue-generic and is correctly absent from this account rather than omitted by oversight. For most of the other listed factors (HSF4, PHF20, TFDP2, THAP1, ZNF135, HOXD10, HES1, KDM5B, EP300) the literature was thin, off-topic, or unplaced in one or both diseases, and they are not part of this specific programme.
